language.script: Kanji (Chinese characters) mixed with Hiragana and Katakana syllabaries — three scripts used together in ordinary text

terrainDescription.zh: 多山列島地形，平原稀少且高度都市化，山地占國土約七成，沿海為主要聚落帶
terrainDescription.en: A mountainous archipelago with limited flat land; roughly 70% of the terrain is mountainous, so settlement concentrates in dense coastal plains

plate.color: white background/green text (private ≥660cc); green background/white text (commercial ≥660cc); yellow background/black text (private kei cars ≤660cc); black background/yellow text (commercial kei cars)

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Highly varied by region rather than one national standard; a recurring feature is a circular protruding reflector, and yellow-and-black diagonal stripes are common on pole-mounted hazard markers

utilityPole.transformerMount: Tapered grey concrete poles, often with a cylindrical drum-shaped transformer partway up; crossbar/insulator style varies by region (e.g. a tuning-fork-shaped pole top is common in the Kansai region)

historicalContext.zh: 漢字自古代由中國傳入日本，之後發展出平假名與片假名兩套表音文字，三者混用是日文書寫最鮮明的視覺特徵。
historicalContext.en: Kanji (Chinese characters) were imported from China in antiquity; Hiragana and Katakana syllabaries were later developed domestically — the mix of all three is Japanese writing's most visually distinctive trait.
